body:
Maxima’s food ledger rescanned the entire residual grid to validate its summed-area cache for every candidate site, making the all-sites pass quadratic in map area. Prepare the table once per evaluated result and retain its buffers between planning passes; bounds become constant-time reads. Snapshot ownership also fixes stale bounds when wheat moves without changing total supply.

No core movement/harvesting rules or serialized formats change. Maxima can choose differently where the old cache was stale. The existing tournament test also gets the correct Windows SDL entry-point signature so CI can link it.

| Paired workload | Before CPU | Final CPU | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| macOS, eight mixed AIs, 256², 12,000 ticks, checksums and saves | 145.99 s | 63.20 s | 56.7% |
| Linux, same initial save, 4096 ticks, final save only | 48.25 s | 12.36 s | 74.4% |

The 512² isolated ledger benchmark’s evaluation plus full-map query pass fell from 11.43 CPU seconds to 3.31 milliseconds. All benchmark digests match at 128², 256² and 512². This kernel factor is not a full-game speedup.

Validation:
- All 12,000 per-tick records and final save bytes match the original macOS build. Final macOS/Linux builds also match all 12,000 per-tick records, including entity diagnostics and populations.
- Independent wrapped-grid oracle, snapshot/copy/reset regressions, full Maxima integration, and ASan/UBSan pass. Old code fails the new equal-total relocation regression. The ledger suite now runs in Linux CI.
- Four-Maxima continuation matches uninterrupted execution on macOS/Linux. The mixed-game tick-6000 checkpoint still diverges at tick 6005; the original macOS and Linux binaries reproduce that existing issue. This PR does not fix it.
- All seven CI jobs passed on engine/test commit `524ab96b4`. Windows per-tick execution was not measured. The final commit only attaches artifacts, removes the temporary performance document, and tidies the test README.

Evidence: [retained inputs, checkpoints, final save, commands, hashes, per-tick digests, profiles and test logs](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/937912187/test/fixtures/maxima-food-ledger/validation-20260914.tar.gz), with a [SHA-256 member index](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/937912187/test/fixtures/maxima-food-ledger/validation-20260914.index.json). Extract into an empty directory with `tar -xzf`. Full multi-gigabyte sidecars and executables remain local; the included parser regenerates the compact per-tick digests. Baseline source is `781e6c0f5`; exact binary/source/input hashes are in the archive.

Limits: these are seeded pilots on a busy host, not universal speedups. The longer macOS pair’s peak RSS increased from 319.86 to 1166.66 MiB despite buffer reuse; the shorter Linux pair stayed near 131 MiB. The macOS residency difference is not isolated, and concurrent-match capacity is not claimed to improve. An unrelated existing fertility test’s 100 ms wall-time assertion failed at 313 ms on the busy macOS host; scoped correctness and integration checks pass. No interactive play session was performed.

Reprofiling the final build leaves engine gradients (~41%), Maxima placement (~22%), and Cortex spatial work (~15%) as the largest spatial categories in a 10-second opening window. Residual cache preparation is no longer a sampled hotspot.
title: Eliminate quadratic Maxima food-ledger cache checks
